proposed_facts.reason: The accessor exposes x1A4C. The replacement writer raises accumulated fields before capping the separate balance; the award writer performs u32 addition, stores it, and subsequently performs guarded raising. Figure-pon subtracts ten through the replacement API. The proposed text correctly rejects overflow saturation without asserting compiled boundary behavior.

The accessor is address-only. Unsigned addition followed by comparison against the unsigned maximum cannot detect overflow, so the award writer does not establish global monotonicity. The proposal preserves the narrower guarded-replacement behavior and separate spending path.

The complete selector has only controller < PAD_MAX_CONTROLLERS in the sentinel branch, with no lower-bound check. The other branch ignores controller and uses unchecked signed quotient/remainder indexing by nineteen.

The setter overwrites the same table read by CF5C. Event-menu code renders that value either as frame-derived time or as an integer. Removing Time is a meaningful supported improvement; the proposed spelling remains an inferred name.

The destination x0 is declared u32, and its unsigned sum cannot exceed -1U. The 0x1388 threshold and separate check-before-set x4/x5/x6 latches are explicit. The proposal appropriately avoids asserting VS-only provenance or a complete Score Display mapping.

The parameterless void function compound-ANDs the explicitly declared u8 x186C with 0xFFFFFFFB. This clears mask four while preserving the other stored bits; the literal does not make the destination 32-bit.

contradictions.reason: Accept the two coin supersessions. Preserve aliasing, separate-balance accounting and guarded raising, but reject saturation and universal monotonicity. The restored wrapper bodies also substantiate the lottery bridge mentioned as missing by the bounded link shards; those historical deferrals are not interpreted as a denial of this newly examined bridge. No link mutation is proposed.

Accept the selector-range correction and retain the handicap-related deferrals. The reset loop writes five only through non-null pointers; its six iterations do not establish six successful fallback writes. Numeric rule value one, the neutral interpretation of five, and overlay mode identities require separate evidence. The rendered AutoHandicap name cannot establish those meanings.

Accept the Event setter rename. Accept the separate Event progression, marker-color, exit-provenance and special-latch deferrals: table presentation establishes time-or-integer records, not red markers, accessible-group expansion, an identity mapping through gm_801BEBC0, successful final-event clearing, or no-falls semantics. The unconditional latch setter does not prove those caller qualifications. The deferred Discord-backed exit link is not needed to support the rename.

Accept rejection of the Classic saturation assertion and the three Adventure score deferrals. Greater-only unsigned comparison is supported, not a nonnegative signed-storage invariant. The aggregate additions occur before their casts, so replacing saturation with an unconditional signed-wrapping guarantee would also overstate the C. Preserve independently supported record access and update behavior.

Accept all Classic, case-22 and All-Star difficulty/stock deferrals. The caller raises CPU-level records and replaces stocks when the old value is zero or the candidate is lower, under level four. It does not exclude zero candidates, prove once-only initialization or permanence after one, establish remaining-stock provenance, or map four to Very Hard. Reductions start at four, so their result is bounded by that initializer. Field names do not authenticate three-bit declarations or compiled conversion behavior. Direct setters are not intrinsic minimum operations.

Accept completion-state, mode-dispatch and challenger-mapping deferrals, including the initially-clear qualification for the All-Star mask query. OR-setting preserves prior state; a query need not be zero before a repeated update. Numeric dispatch cases, enum spellings, thresholds and local flags alone do not authenticate terminal-success semantics, complete roster classification, Marth/Young Link encounter dispatch or accomplishment text. Preserve the upstream index-three exclusion and distinct-count qualifications. Historical Classic/Adventure/All-Star caller-link deferrals remain bounded provenance limitations, not rejections of retained mode-family knowledge elsewhere.

Accept all four x1C Classic-clear rejections. The getter only queries x1C. Both the stage-specific Classic branch and the separate course-result handler write it, so the rendered GetClassicClearFlag and Classic Mode clear descriptions are misleading. Preserve the separate fighter flag, x4 and x8 completion stores. Accept the remaining Target Test scene/ground-helper and named-trophy deferrals: the observed writes and frame comparisons do not alone establish every gameplay or reward identity.

Accept both Multi-Man score/time reversals as rejected. Set b2 restores x4 and returns; clear b2 restores x2 and supplies the sentinel to the x4 path. The set-state saved record is formatted as frame time. Accept the separate arbitrary-input Boolean/ABI deferral: direct assignment of s32 to a packed field is not general nonzero normalization.

Accept the remaining Multi-Man objective, score-unit, variant and display-chain deferrals. Persistent record restoration/saving, timed setup and named query wrappers support the documented record families, but do not prove exact opponent objectives, increasing difficulty, survival requirements or KO termination. Incidental restored wrappers support portions of the deferred 10-Man and Cruel chains; this does not turn all historical caller explanations into independently authenticated complete gameplay claims.

Accept Home-Run and Training unit/provenance deferrals, including the broader auxiliary-progress-record claims. The two Home-Run accessors select distinct fields and must not inherit units from each other. The restored Training updater confirms parallel maxima and its accessor bridge, but not the measurement producer's consecutive-hit identity or reward meanings. Likewise, the restored Home-Run wrapper alone does not authenticate the full runtime serialization and localized display chain.

Accept notification, trophy-registration and bonus-family deferrals. The code distinguishes registration bits, paired marker bits and timestamps; a conditional registration is not a once-per-lifetime guarantee when guards can be cleared. IsFeatureUnlocked is broader than the demonstrated registration domain. Numeric entry/category/reward IDs, bulk loops and forwarding wrappers do not establish every message category, trophy identity, collection-exposure effect, debug origin, end-of-match origin or presentation lifecycle. Raw base-plus-0x6C timestamp arithmetic also does not authenticate compiled equivalence to the named member. Preserve retained consumer findings from the other research shards without using rendered names as evidence.

Accept both name-reference net-effect deferrals. Deletion calls the adjustment routine, but unk_1490 is visited twice by a non-idempotent helper. A reference one above the deleted index may first decrement and then clear; larger references may decrement twice. Rules-sentinel preservation also requires the deleted index not to equal the sentinel. Maintenance intent and the supported name-management relationship stand; universal identity preservation and a compiled explanation of the duplicate do not.

Accept BGM, Sound Test and sound-balance deferrals. The BGM body supports short-circuit predicates and numeric alternatives, not independently authenticated track identities, complete-unlock meanings or random distribution. The music setter merely stores its argument; audio-query looping eligibility or playback acceptance requires that query's semantics. Saved sound-balance access and menu stepping do not by themselves establish endpoint muting. Historical music-chain links remain deferred without contradicting the retained carryover findings.

Accept the two Deflicker fact and two Deflicker link alias deferrals, together with the settings-field and preview-timing qualifications. The setter writes deflicker; the saved selection getter calls GetRumbleSettingOfPort(5), whose body indexes rumble_enabled. Neighboring declarations and rendered Deflicker names cannot prove byte equivalence. Video selection and configuration submission are supported, but immediate submission must not be conflated with immediate hardware application. No deferred layout or synchronization question was researched to manufacture a resolution.

Accept the counter-saturation and mask-width supersessions. Accept the related Additional Rules, VS-only accounting, Score Display prerequisite and in-match presentation deferrals. The threshold/latches, registration-entry reconciliation and availability bits are distinct from an active match rule. Restored numeric table connections establish useful portions of the chain, but not all player-facing identities or all accounting callers. The broader rendered AdditionalRules name therefore remains a hypothesis rather than proof.

Accept all remaining counter-arithmetic deferrals: Coin, reset, Stamina, Stock, Time, self-destruct, elapsed-time, damage and auxiliary progression descriptions must not infer saturation from a post-addition maximum comparison. Preserve the result-selector 7/8 bypass and Stamina precedence. Signed expressions and unsigned expressions must be analyzed separately; no blanket compiled wrapping claim is substituted for the unsupported saturation guarantees.

Accept records-definition, display and lifetime deferrals: Bonus victory criteria, exact localized labels, unrestricted match-count definitions, damage-event provenance, self-destruct event definitions, included single-player/Versus modes, combined human-player-hours and Mewtwo thresholds, platform-specific Power Count conditions, and exhaustive Power Time screen coverage exceed accessor and immediate-updater evidence. The contestant total is cumulative rather than an average, but the inherited display-cap qualification must remain. Records-menu versus character-selection record indicators is a genuine concept-boundary question. These deferrals preserve, rather than erase, supported aliases and records-row associations.

Accept all compiled-section and structure-layout deferrals, including source-object addresses/order, .bss/.data/.sdata/.sdata2 membership, literal alignment, shared selection-record size, auxiliary mask offsets, counter trailing padding and exact bitmap capacity. Source declarations and initializers establish authored objects, not emitted section layout. Preserve the explicit x4C[4]-plus-padding and name-bank extent discrepancies instead of normalizing them to logical caller domains. The nineteen reset assignments prove field zeroing, not a byte-complete zero object or a compiled 0x44-byte extent.

Accept persistent-profile, settings, shared-statistics and reset-purpose deferrals. Mutable aliases, name indexing, rumble initialization and selected reset operations are supported, but they do not independently establish every per-name rumble consumer, damage statistic, cumulative-field interpretation, full localization mapping or VS Records UI category. Manager reset storage does not alone prove common game-mode initialization placement. Preserve supported retained profile, settings, card and records knowledge without treating one shard's missing consumer as a global contradiction.

Accept deletion-category, reset-helper, trophy-recovery and startup deferrals. The owned bodies establish clear operations, ordered helper calls, bank reconstruction, status guards, language-value assignments and runtime bookkeeping. They do not establish every delegated unlock/Toy/category effect, deletion confirmation or label, scan-helper meaning, normal/debug read-result provenance, JP/US mapping, startup ordering or actual intro skipping. Preserve the inherited warning that Toy work can precede the cited reset, and do not use rendered helper names to fill missing effects. Trophy category commit semantics and the count-to-interface bridge remain explicitly deferred.

Accept remaining deferred concept links and broad TU mapping as bounded research limitations. Missing or shifted historical caller ranges, unverified Discord/wiki provenance, numeric scene/option/award identities and incomplete intermediary chains justify deferral, not automatic rejection or adoption. This includes character-unlock retry difficulty, Random Stage Switch/Sound Test menu consumers, progressive-selection lifecycle, frontend notification presentation, and broad persistent-game-data/Records relationships. Supported mechanics and all unchanged retained research rows are inherited verbatim. Restored evidence authenticates some intermediary portions, but no new full audit or link replacement is claimed.

The duplicate unk_1490 name-reference adjustment, Deflicker indexed-byte equivalence, positive-stock invariants and numeric difficulty/feature mappings remain qualified as described in the independent reconciliation.

evidence.why: Shows the matching b0 setter and aggregation over 25 fighter records.

evidence.why: Shows the pointer-rooted save and subrecord access, but not compiled section membership.

link_dispositions.reason: Source-level pointer-based save access does not authenticate the compiled .sdata target or its placement. Unsupported compiled layout remains unresolved.

baseline_record.why: The function exposes a mutable field embedded in the central save-data record, making that persistent value available to accounting code while preserving the record's owning layout behind the game-manager API.

evidence.why: Returns a mutable field address through GetSaveData.

link_dispositions.reason: The function directly returns the address of x1A44 in the central save record, supporting the persistent-game-data relationship without assigning that field a more specific meaning.

baseline_record.why: Character-unlock selection directly consumes this completion query when evaluating the ten-character Young Link condition and the all-character Mr. Game & Watch condition.

evidence.why: Defines the indexed x10 completion-bit query.
Completion aggregation and the ten-completion selection consume the query.
The aggregate predicate gates selection of the locked CKIND_GAMEWATCH character.

link_dispositions.reason: The indexed bit query is consumed both by the completion-count condition selecting CKIND_CLINK and by the aggregate predicate selecting CKIND_GAMEWATCH. The latter explicitly excludes index 3 rather than literally testing every index.

baseline_record.why: The function maps a logical saved-name slot to the persistent `NameTagData` record containing that player-name profile's retained data.

evidence.why: Maps a logical name index to a NameTagData entry in persistent save data.
The same bank indexing addresses records whose namedata receives name strings and whose rumble_enabled field is initialized.

link_dispositions.reason: The canonical accessor returns the persistent NameTagData record selected by quotient and remainder modulo 19. Initialization of the same bank entries copies name strings into namedata and enables rumble, supporting the player-name profile association.

baseline_record.why: The function marks a trophy for the pending prize flow that installs and presents its collection state.

evidence.why: Contains the complete setter, matching bitmap query, and persistent-bit accessors used by the prize flow.
Prize entry queries the runtime bitmap for trophy indices, timestamps and records newly encountered entries, invokes Toy_SetUnlockState, and constructs prize records.

link_dispositions.reason: The setter and gmMainLib_8015DA1C operate on the same runtime bitmap. The prize-entry flow tests that bitmap across TY_TROPHY_COUNT, updates persistent recording and unlock state when necessary, and queues prize entries. This supports the trophy-collection link without claiming that the setter itself installs or presents a trophy.
